2: Classic controls dynamics with a fixed ratio in dB; Super uses the original QQ curve. Compressor offers single, upward and dual compression. Clipper provides downward compression only, while Limiter adds a Ceiling for final peak control. In ST, L/R Link and M/S Link adjust left/right or mid/side coupling with one set of parameters. The Quick Start introduces both controls.
4: Start with Compressor / ST, then choose another mode if needed.
5: CLASSIC, SINGLE, ST, SC: INT; Lookahead 26 ms, Window 26 ms, SAFE off and OS 1x.
7: L/R Link and M/S Link both default to 100%. Lower the first to blend in independent left/right compression, or the second for independent mid/side compression. You still use one set of knobs. See pages 21-22.
9: Use Threshold to choose where processing begins. Increase Ratio from 1:1, then use Mix to set the amount.
10: Play representative material, click Match, then listen to attacks, tails and placement in the mix.
12: Read the Clipper and Limiter workflows. Understand L/R Link first, then compare Window, loudness and dynamics.
14: Use Bypass or A/B to compare. A louder result is not necessarily a better one.
15: Interface, three processing modes and basic operation
17: ST L/R Link and M/S Link
18: ST / LR / MS and parameter LINK
19: Clipper: downward compression, L/R Link and GR hold
22: Mode and the two ST Link values, followed by SAFE, Lookahead + Window, then Monitor + OS. Clipper / Limiter use L/R Link in the first row and have no channel Monitor.
23: Cycle through COMPRESSOR / CLIPPER / LIMITER, then choose FULL / ECO, sidechain, theme, A/B and Bypass.
25: The top button selects Compressor / Clipper / Limiter.
26: Click the leftmost processing-mode button to cycle Compressor → Clipper → Limiter.
27: The processing mode determines which features are available. Compressor handles general dynamics. Clipper focuses on downward compression at higher ratios. Limiter adds a Ceiling after dynamics processing to control final peaks.
29: Switch from Compressor to Clipper and back, and your previous Compressor settings return. Each A/B snapshot also stores all three sets of mode parameters. See page 44.
31: In Compressor, the lower-right Mode button cycles ST → LR → MS → ST. ST uses one set of parameters; LR lets you adjust left and right separately; MS lets you adjust mid and side separately. This is a different choice from the top processing-mode button.
33: ST L/R Link and M/S Link both default to 100%. Lower either value to try more independent processing without switching to the two sets of knobs in LR / MS. See pages 21-22.
36: Upward, downward or dual compression. Offers ST / LR / MS; ST has two numeric Link controls for coupling.
37: Downward only, Ratio 10:1-1000:1. One set of parameters and L/R Link, without dual compression or Ceiling.
38: One set of parameters and L/R Link. Offers single / dual compression, Ceiling, TP and level-matched monitoring.
39: Classic and Super both use -90 to 0 dB for Threshold, UP and DOWN. Super no longer offers -inf. Rectangle zoom changes only the visible Display range, not the threshold value; see page 16.
40: On this page, 'no compression' means no dynamic cut or boost. Input, Makeup, Mix and Output Gain still apply. EXT uses the external sidechain level for these decisions. Clipper and Limiter do not use Range; see pages 30-33.
41: Clipper / Limiter use a different link
42: The normal Input / Output LINK applies equal and opposite gain changes; it does not replace Match. It is hidden and inactive in Clipper / Limiter. Their LINK beside Output couples the downward threshold and output in opposite directions. It defaults off in Clipper and on in Limiter; see page 44.
43: Choose the processing mode and Limiter headphone state first. Play representative, non-silent material. Once valid loudness data is available, you can click Match during playback.
44: Stopping retains the result; the next playback starts a new measurement. If playback does not stop, loops and jumps remain part of the same Match measurement.
45: Comp / Clipper compare Dry with Wet before Makeup. Limiter headphone mode compares the original input with the actual limited monitor output, then writes one shared Makeup value. Clicking Match or adjusting Makeup does not reset the measurement start.
46: Changing processing mode or the Limiter headphone state changes the measurement reference and clears the statistics, so choose them before playback. Silence or insufficient data cannot be matched. To compare only the new settings, stop and replay the same material.
47: Adjusts Wet level before Mix: Comp ±30 dB; Clipper / Limiter ±120 dB.
48: Comp ±24 dB; Clipper / Limiter ±120 dB. Headphone monitoring: pages 37-38.
49: Algorithms, single / dual mode, thresholds, Ratio, UP / DOWN switches, gains, Mix, Lookahead, SAFE, Window, global OS and sidechain; also the active processing mode, TP, Ceiling, TP recovery, Link states and all three sets of processing parameters.
50: Display: drag to zoom into detail
51: All three processing modes use the same zoom controls.
52: Display shows level and gain references over time. To inspect a passage or smaller level changes, hold the left mouse button inside the graph, drag a rectangle and release.
53: Draw a rectangle around the time and level range you want to enlarge.
54: Release to zoom in. Playback keeps scrolling at the selected zoom scale.
55: Zoom the view, keep the thresholds
56: The fader scales on the right follow the graph. Existing Threshold, UP, DOWN and Range values stay unchanged. An off-screen threshold retains its readout; right-click to restore the full view. Zoom does not change the sound, compression amount or latency.
57: Grey is the input reference; blue / green indicate cut / boost; orange is the output reference. Curves follow the current settings, including while dragging Window or HPF. HPF UPDATING means calculation is still in progress. Display is a level reference, not a recording of the final waveform.
58: In Limiter, the input reference and output after Ceiling are aligned to the same time position. The external sidechain curve is independent of Window and SAFE; HPF / Key Gain change that curve.
61: Zoom into the selected time and level range together.
63: The view keeps scrolling at the chosen scale; it does not freeze on the selected audio.
65: Restore the full view: 8 seconds of history, 0 to -90 dB.
66: Compare Lookahead 40 ms / Window 26 ms with Lookahead 26 ms / Window 26 ms. With other parameters identical, settings settled and latency aligned, the dynamics core produces the same compression and harmonic coloration. The first setting simply retains 14 ms more base latency. This lets you audition a shorter effective Lookahead without repeatedly changing plugin latency.
68: Two ST Links, one set of parameters
69: Understand left/right and mid/side, then adjust their coupling.
70: Comp / ST: L/R Link and M/S Link appear together beside Mode. Both default to 100%.
71: L/R means left and right channels; M/S means mid and side signals. Mid reflects what the channels share, while Side reflects their difference. They are two ways of describing the same stereo material.
72: Link controls how closely compression is coupled
73: At 100% / 100%, both sides share compression gain, preserving the original ST behavior. Lowering Link still uses one set of Ratio, threshold, Makeup and Mix controls; no second set of knobs appears.
76: Set the basic sound with Ratio, Threshold and Mix.
77: Adjust one Link at a time
78: Leave the other at 100%. Gradually lower L/R Link or M/S Link and compare attacks, tails, the center and width.
80: Once you can hear each change clearly, adjust both. The next page gives four starting points.
81: Double-click to enter a percentage; drag vertically to adjust, with Shift for finer changes. Alt-click (Option on Mac) resets to 100%.
83: Blends in independently compressed left/right results, giving each channel's own dynamics more influence.
84: Blends in independently compressed mid/side results, giving the center and sides' dynamics more influence.
86: These values blend processing results; they are not channel volume controls.
87: Both Links at 0%: combine independent L/R and M/S processing with one set of controls.
89: With M/S Link at 100%, lowering L/R Link gradually moves from shared gain toward independent left/right compression. Lowering both blends in independent left/right and independent mid/side results together.
90: The values are not volume percentages and do not need to add up to 100%. This is not L/R compression followed by another M/S compressor in series. The two values determine how the processing results are combined.
91: Numeric Link and parameter LINK are different
92: These two values change the coupling of audio processing. In LR / MS, the LINK button beside Mode moves two sets of parameters together; it does not force both sides to use identical compression gain.
93: When should you switch to LR / MS?
94: Choose LR / MS when left/right or mid/side need different Ratio, threshold, Makeup or Mix settings. Stay in ST if you only want to adjust coupling while keeping one shared set of parameters.
95: Lowering Link can change the stereo image and width. Use Match for a similar-loudness comparison, then check the full mix. Neither 100% nor 0% is a fixed answer for every source.
97: Original ST behavior, with shared compression gain.
98: Independent left/right compression, using the same parameters for both channels.
99: Independent mid/side compression, using the same parameters for mid and side.
100: Equal parts independent left/right and independent mid/side processing.
101: ST and LR: shared or separate controls
102: In Compressor, the lower-right Mode button cycles ST → LR → MS → ST. Start with ST; choose LR when you need separate settings for each side. Clipper and Limiter omit this selector and use one ST-style graph, one set of parameters and a numeric L/R Link. All three Mode buttons share the same size; LR / MS place parameter LINK directly to the right.
103: One set of parameters. With both numeric Links at 100%, compression gain is shared. Lower them to blend in independent left/right or mid/side compression.
104: Numeric Link values and LINK buttons
105: ST L/R Link and M/S Link control audio coupling; the LINK button beside Mode moves two sets of parameters together. The small LINK between the Ratios couples Up / Down inversely. Mode LINK couples matching L/R or M/S parameters. With both buttons on, channels move together while each channel retains its Up / Down relationship. Input LINK only applies opposite input/output gain changes; see page 13.
107: One set of parameters and L/R Link, without Ceiling.
108: CLIPPER has no dual compression or Ceiling. LINK beside Output defaults off.
109: Clipper uses the Classic / Super dynamics algorithms for downward compression only. Ratio ranges from 10:1 to 1000:1, letting you compare stronger compression's effect on peaks, density and tone. Lookahead, Window, SAFE, Mix and OS remain available.
111: Clipper has no final Ceiling protection. Use Limiter's Ceiling when you need a final peak limit. Clipper's threshold readout is not an output ceiling after subsequent gain adjustments.
113: 10:1-1000:1; default and Alt reset: 10:1. The arc is unlit at the far left to show the minimum setting.
114: 0%-100%; default and Alt reset: 0%. Left and right can act independently; increase the value for more coupling.
115: Off by default: threshold, Makeup and Output adjust independently. Enable it for equal and opposite linked changes.
117: Downward only. No dual mode, Range, Ceiling, channel Monitor or ST / LR / MS selector.
118: Clipper: Window, coupling and GR hold
119: Listen first; use GR to see the deepest reduction during this playback.
121: Choose Classic or Super, start Ratio at 10:1 and gradually lower Threshold. Keep Output LINK off; adjust Makeup or Output independently as needed for a level comparison.
123: Keep Lookahead at 26 ms and shorten Window to compare peaks, density and coloration. SAFE is greyed out at Window 0. If that sound works best, consider switching to 0 ms Lookahead.
124: Adjust how the channels influence each other
125: Start L/R Link at its default 0% for independent left/right compression. Increase it for more shared attenuation, listening to the image and dynamics as you adjust.
127: For short Window settings or deep compression, compare 4x / 8x / 16x. OS defaults to 1x and is your choice. Finish with a similar-loudness comparison using Match, Bypass or A/B.
129: Clipper holds the deepest GR reached by each channel during the current playback. It updates only when reduction goes deeper, and remains held after stopping. Makeup and Output Gain are excluded from this reduction value.
131: Double-clicking GR clears only the reduction history. Double-click the top TP number to clear the true-peak hold. Maximum GR does not mean that amount is applied continuously; listen to the changing dynamics too.
134: Retains maximum reduction without automatic decay.
136: Clears both channels' GR and starts accumulating again.
138: Resets automatically and records this new playback.
139: One ST graph and shared parameters. Drag a rectangle to zoom into detail; threshold scales follow the graph. Limiter does not use Range.
140: UP remains independent of Output Gain and Makeup, even with Output LINK on. Drag a rectangle to zoom Display; right-click to restore the full view. UP cannot exceed DOWN, and zoom does not rewrite thresholds.
141: Complete downward compression on page 33, or add gentle upward compression on page 34, then enable headphones. Keep Ceiling and TP settings unchanged and turn SC LISTEN off. Limiter outputs full stereo.
142: Every click measures from the start of this playback, without clearing history or stacking the previous correction. To compare only new settings, stop and replay before Match. Makeup's correction may be limited with Limiter LINK off, at parameter limits, or with a fully dry Mix.
145: Range cannot fall below Threshold; DOWN cannot fall below UP. They move together on contact, and dynamic processing stops when they coincide. Clipper / Limiter do not use Range. Dual UP is always independent of Output / Makeup linking.
146: Defaults: Comp Single Threshold and Dual UP start at -90 dB. Dual DOWN and Clipper / Limiter Single Threshold start at 0 dB. Alt-click resets Threshold and UP to -90 dB, and DOWN to 0 dB; enabled LINK still respects shared limits.
147: Cycles through the modes; each stores its own parameters.
148: Compressor / Limiter dual mode can select separate UP and DOWN algorithms.
152: Downward only. Default / Alt: 10:1; no lit arc at minimum.
153: Comp up to 200; Limiter UP up to 8, DOWN up to 1000
154: Default 1:1; Clipper has no dual mode.
155: Independent dual switches retain their Ratio values.
156: Display scales follow zoom; stored values stay unchanged.
157: Comp Single only; no compression at or above this level.
159: LINK beside LR / MS couples the two sets of parameters.
162: Default / Alt: 0%; one set of parameters.
164: Links UP / DOWN inversely; initially ON.
165: Each processing mode retains its gain, detector and timing settings; see page 44. ECO transport suspension, hidden-editor analysis and FULL low-residual sleep are covered on pages 48-49.
167: Available only in Comp LR / MS.
168: Disabled at Lookahead or Window 0 ms.
170: Default Compressor; Limiter TP defaults ON
171: TP and Ceiling are available only in Limiter.
172: Threshold defines the gain curve at the detected level, not a floor for the final output. Quieter parts within a Window also receive gain determined by that peak. Shared gain with both ST Links at 100%, an external sidechain or HPF can also make the detected level differ from the visible signal. Makeup and Output Gain further change the output.
173: Right-click Display to restore the full view, then drag a new zoom rectangle if needed. Audio and threshold values outside the view are retained.
174: Three modes, three sets of settings
175: Compressor, Clipper and Limiter store parameters separately.
176: The top button cycles Compressor → Clipper → Limiter. Each mode stores its own Input, Makeup, Mix, Output, algorithms, Ratio, thresholds, sidechain, Lookahead, Window, SAFE and OS. Each starts with its own defaults on first use.
178: Switching A/B restores all three sets of mode parameters in that snapshot, along with the active processing mode. FULL / ECO, headphone 1:1 and channel monitoring are working preferences, independent of A/B.
180: Switching to Dual carries Single Threshold into DOWN; returning to Single carries the current DOWN into Threshold. Each keeps its own Ratio. Input, Makeup, Mix and Output retain their current settings. UP cannot exceed DOWN and is moved to the same position if necessary.
181: Output LINK depends only on its switch
182: Linking still works at Ratio 1:1 or with DOWN off
183: Only Output LINK controls this relationship. Ratio, ON/OFF, Mix, algorithm, Window, OS and other parameters do not affect it. Decreasing values reverses the direction; both controls stop together at a range limit. Dual UP always stays independent. Clipper follows the same rules when LINK is enabled.
184: For example, lowering the downward Threshold from -18 to -20 dB raises Output by 2 dB, even at Ratio 1:1. With LINK off, the controls adjust independently.
188: ST / LR / MS, two ST Link values, Single Range, dual compression and Ratio LINK.
189: Downward only, Ratio 10:1-1000:1 and numeric L/R Link. Output LINK defaults off.
190: Numeric L/R Link, single / dual mode, Ceiling / TP and recovery. Output LINK defaults on.
191: Increase downward Threshold / DOWN by 1 dB
192: Output falls by 1 dB; Makeup stays unchanged.
194: Output falls by 1 dB; threshold stays unchanged.
196: Downward threshold falls by 1 dB; Makeup stays unchanged.
197: OS is in the fourth row at the lower right. Each mode stores its own factor and starts at 1x; old projects retain saved settings.
198: Clipper at a high Ratio and short Window also benefits from comparing OS settings. These are listening suggestions, not a sharp 'distortion-free' boundary at 10 ms. Oversampling mainly reduces aliasing; it does not remove every harmonic or replace SAFE / Window for controlling crackle and anticipatory attenuation.
199: Default for all three modes. No audio oversampling, with lower processing load.
200: OUTPUT / LUFS-I appears at the lower-left of the Display in Clipper and Limiter.
201: LUFS-I measures integrated loudness over a passage; TP measures peaks. They serve different purposes. LUFS-I reads the actual monitor path, including current gain and audition settings. In Limiter, this also includes Ceiling and headphone compensation.
202: A new playback, jump or loop starts a fresh measurement; stopping holds the result. If the host provides no transport state, Clipper / Limiter measure continuously.
203: Play the same passage with identical SC LISTEN and headphone states. Clipper / Limiter output full stereo and have no channel MONITOR. Turn headphones and SC LISTEN off when judging the normal signal sent downstream.
206: Click SAFE to turn it on (yellow); click again to turn it off (unlit). Window and latency stay unchanged. The on/off state is saved with the project and A/B.
208: With Lookahead 26 ms / Window 0 ms, detection uses the current sample but retains 26 ms of lookahead latency. Lookahead 0 ms removes that delay and fixes Window at 0. Both cases give identical Normal/Safe detection: SAFE is disabled and greyed out, retaining its on/off choice. It becomes available when both values exceed 0 ms. OS and Limiter Ceiling may still add latency.
210: Threshold sets the level where processing begins. At or below it, there is no compression; above it, Ratio determines downward attenuation or upward gain. Its range is -90 to 0 dB; Comp Single defaults to -90 dB.
211: UP: -90 dB. DOWN: 0 dB. The defaults are the same for Classic and Super.
212: If either side would exceed its range, both stop where their difference can be retained. For example, thresholds of -80 / -70 dB can be lowered together to -90 / -80 dB. Classic and Super follow the same rule.
215: New Compressor instances remember the last manually selected algorithm; projects and A/B restore their saved choice. Clipper and Limiter keep separate settings. A short crossfade reduces transients when changing algorithms.
216: Thresholds below -90 dB in old projects, presets and A/B slots, including -inf, are recalled as -90 dB. Range OFF is retained: it removes the upper processing limit and remains different from 0 dB.
217: Old ST loads with 100% L/R Link; old LR / MS with 0%. Thresholds below -90 dB, including -inf, become -90 dB; other saved thresholds remain. Old Range no longer applies. Values previously set to -45 dB cannot be recovered automatically. The old L settings (M for MS) become shared controls; old MS now processes left/right. Different old channel settings may change the sound, so check by ear. Compressor LR / MS is unchanged.
219: Restore the control's reset value; see page 40 for thresholds. Linked controls follow within their shared limits.
226: Classic and Super use the same ranges and reset values. With LINK on, resets respect the shared control limits. Range OFF is retained: processing continues above Threshold.
228: Thresholds below -90 dB in old projects, presets and A/B slots, including old -inf values, load as -90 dB. Other valid thresholds retain their saved values.
